prize_parts.citation: for the development of general palladium-catalyzed carbon-nitrogen cross-coupling

statement.case_for: Palladium-catalyzed C-N cross-coupling is the cleanest case on the shortlist on all three tests. The discovery is a general, predictable catalytic method rather than a single reaction. It rests on ligand design and mechanistic understanding that Buchwald and Hartwig built independently and in parallel. After more than 25 years it is used at industrial scale in pharmaceutical, agrochemical and materials synthesis, so independent confirmation and impact are not in doubt. Three of eight of us ranked it first, which tells me the scientific case is broadly recognisable. I would still defend it on merit rather than on that count. A two-person prize also avoids the forced omissions that burden most other candidates, where credit has to be cut from five to eight names.
statement.case_against: The strongest objection is that the 2010 prize for Pd-catalyzed cross-coupling (Heck, Negishi, Suzuki) already covered this territory, so the committee could see C-N coupling as a downstream extension and not a new concept. Kosugi's earlier tin-amide coupling is a legitimate precursor, and the Buchwald-Hartwig ligand generations are individually contestable. The reaction is also a synthetic-methodology tool, and the committee may prefer a discovery that opens a new field. I think the general ligand-controlled catalytic amination is distinct enough, but this is the point on which a majority could turn against it.

responses.point: Johan ranks B065 first with Hartwig and Buchwald, and also argues strongly for B032 (energy landscape theory of folding, Wolynes, Onuchic, Bryngelson) as a very mature conceptual framework underlying folding, binding and design.
responses.response: I agree on B065 and on the Kosugi precursor point. On B032 I disagree on timing and attribution, not on quality. The funnel concept is deeply influential, but after the 2024 prize for structure prediction and design it risks looking like a retrospective supplement. The third name is also unstable, because Dill and Fersht have strong claims, so the three-person set is less secure than the Buchwald-Hartwig pair. I would not move B032 above B065, but I take seriously that it is the most conceptually fundamental candidate on the shortlist.

responses.point: Heiner ranks massively parallel sequencing (B037) first with Balasubramanian, Klenerman and Mayer, calling the impact exceptional and the recognition arguably overdue.
responses.response: This is my own second choice and I share the view of its impact, since all of my genome-stability work depends on it. Two reservations remain. First, I would not add Mayer as a third name, because the Solexa chemistry (reversible terminators on clonal clusters) is the decisive invention, and Rothberg and Ju represent parallel routes that a third seat would only invite. The defensible core is Balasubramanian and Klenerman. Second, the committee has to decide whether this is chemistry or genomics technology. Because I use the method daily, I may over-weight its importance, so I do not rank it above B065, where the chemistry is unmistakably the achievement.

responses.point: Peter also ranks B065 first with Buchwald and Hartwig, judging it overdue, and ranks photoredox catalysis (B033) second with Yoon, Stephenson and Nicewicz.
responses.response: I agree with the two-person B065 attribution. Credit for individual ligand generations is a manageable detail and does not change who made the general method. I am less convinced by B033. Credit is spread across Yoon, Stephenson, Nicewicz, MacMillan, König, Melchiorre and Fukuzumi, and MacMillan's 2021 prize for organocatalysis makes a photoredox prize without him look artificial. That attribution problem is more serious than the one in B065, so as a combined prize I would not pair it with B065.

responses.point: Daniel ranks targeted protein degradation (B026) first with Crews, Deshaies and Ciulli, arguing that it turns chemically induced proximity into a general drug modality and explains thalidomide-class drugs.
responses.response: The concept is original and I rank B026 as my third alternative. My difficulty is attribution and maturity. The PROTAC and cereblon-glue strands have different discoverers (Handa and Ito for cereblon), so any three names split one honestly joint field. No PROTAC drug has been approved yet, so the effect on medicine rests on candidates, not outcomes. I would wait for approval before placing it above a field with 25 years of confirmed use.

uncertainties: Whether the committee treats C-N coupling as sufficiently distinct from the 2010 Pd cross-coupling prize.
Whether Kosugi's tin-amide work, together with Migita's, should alter the two-name allocation.
Whether massively parallel sequencing is judged to be chemistry, and whether the pair or a trio is the right allocation.
Whether the committee is willing to wait for PROTAC approval before honoring targeted protein degradation.
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict is apparent from my profile. My research field of nucleotide metabolism and genome stability makes me a heavy user of sequencing (B037), and I have a collaborator in the replication-fidelity community, but I have no personal or institutional tie to any candidate named on the shortlist that would require recusal.
